summary: Recce currently has ZERO Jenkins-JNLP coverage on the raw TCP agent-listener channel. Port 50000/tcp is already claimed by services/db/db2.py (Db2 LUW default) and svcdetect.py contains no JNLP signature — a Jenkins controller answering on 50000 will therefore be mis-fingerprinted as Db2 (or left "unknown" when DRDA EXCSAT fails). HTTP-side Jenkins is well-covered in services/web/checks.py and services/http.py (Groovy Script Console, /jenkins fingerprint, X-Jenkins header, CVE-2024-23897 CLI file-read advisory, act/exploitplan.py Metasploit mapping) but none of that reaches the agent port, and the agent port is the deserialization-RCE surface (CLI2-connect, CVE-2017-1000353) plus the agent-secret relay surface. A new services/jenkins_jnlp.py is needed, plus a Db2/JNLP disambiguator (send a text nudge, JNLP replies "Protocol:" ASCII while Db2/DRDA replies with a binary DSS 0xD0 frame). This module has strong cross-service value: it produces agent NODE NAMES (feed known_users/known_hostnames), the controller's RSA X-Instance-Identity fingerprint (new shared surface for correlating one Jenkins across multiple hosts/ports), and captured HMAC-SHA-256 challenges from JNLP2/3 negotiation (feed known_hashes for hashcat mode 1450). It also consumes the HTTP-side finding stream — if web/checks.py already tagged a host as Jenkins, this module confirms and links the agent port; if this module finds JNLP first, web/checks.py should probe /tcpSlaveAgentListener/ and /instance-identity on the sibling HTTP port to close the loop.
default_ports: 50000/tcp (default, configurable via Configure Global Security -> TCP port for inbound agents)
any port advertised by X-Jenkins-CLI-Port / X-Hudson-CLI-Port response header from the HTTP controller
randomized high port when 'Random' is selected in the controller UI — must be discovered via /tcpSlaveAgentListener/ on the HTTP port

recce/services/serviceenum.py (no jenkins/jnlp entry in _NAME or _PORT — the recce-service.sh driver has no jenkins-agent script to route to)

existing_coverage.notes: Genuinely uncovered. The Db2 module is the only thing that will fire on 50000 today, and its is_db2() returns True for ANY port==50000 without protocol confirmation, so a Jenkins controller on 50000 currently produces a false Db2 finding and no JNLP work. Fixing this is a two-part change: (a) a new jenkins_jnlp.py module, and (b) tightening db2.is_db2()/probe() to REQUIRE the DRDA DSS 0xD0 magic before claiming the port, so JNLP wins when its ASCII 'Protocol:' greeting comes back.

capabilities.name: is-jenkins-jnlp
capabilities.description: Port/service classifier: portid==50000, or servicefp/banner contains 'PROTOCOL_JNLP' / 'Jenkins' / 'jenkins-agent', or nmap named it 'jnlp-agent'/'jenkins'. Mirrors the shape of db2.is_db2()/zk.is_zookeeper(). Must NOT return True on port==50000 alone — see jnlp-vs-db2 disambiguator below.

capabilities.name: jnlp-vs-db2-disambiguator
capabilities.description: Resolve the 50000/tcp collision with services/db/db2.py: open TCP, send b'\r\n', read up to 128 bytes. JNLP controller replies with ASCII 'Protocol:<name> not understood' or lists supported protocols starting with 'PROTOCOL_JNLP'; Db2/DRDA replies with a DSS frame whose 3rd byte is 0xD0 (or times out). Cache the result on port.extrainfo so db2.is_db2() and jnlp.is_jenkins_jnlp() are mutually exclusive. Without this, every Jenkins controller on the default port produces a phantom Db2 finding today.

capabilities.name: jnlp-protocol-negotiation-probe
capabilities.description: Send 'PROTOCOL_INVALID\n' after the initial handshake to trigger the controller's 'supported protocols' error listing. Parses the returned tokens: PROTOCOL_JNLP-connect (v1, plaintext, deprecated), PROTOCOL_JNLP2-connect (plaintext + SHA-based secret), PROTOCOL_JNLP3-connect (SHA + AES), PROTOCOL_JNLP4-connect (TLS-wrapped, current), PROTOCOL_CLI-connect / PROTOCOL_CLI2-connect (legacy CLI over agent port). Emits one finding per legacy protocol still enabled. Analogous to zookeeper.py's 4LW category walk.

capabilities.name: cli2-connect-deserialization-detect
capabilities.description: If PROTOCOL_CLI-connect or PROTOCOL_CLI2-connect appears in the negotiation set, flag CVE-2017-1000353 (pre-auth Java-object deserialization RCE via the CLI over the agent port). Feeds act/exploitplan.py with the Metasploit module exploit/linux/misc/jenkins_command_receive (or exploit/multi/http/jenkins_ldap_deserialize) and a proof-of-exposure runbook. Version-gate against controller banner (fixed in 2.32.2 / 2.46.1) once the sibling HTTP fingerprint is known.

capabilities.name: jnlp-plaintext-secret-leak-detect
capabilities.description: When PROTOCOL_JNLP-connect or PROTOCOL_JNLP2-connect is still enabled, the agent secret + node name traverse the wire in cleartext. Emit high-severity finding — an on-path attacker on the agent LAN passively harvests every reconnecting agent's HMAC secret and replays it. Fixed by disabling JNLP<4 in Configure Global Security.

capabilities.name: http-sibling-tcpSlaveAgentListener-probe
capabilities.description: When the same host has an open Jenkins HTTP port (already fingerprinted by services/web/checks.py and http.py), fetch /tcpSlaveAgentListener/ and read the response headers: X-Jenkins (version), X-Jenkins-Agent-Protocols (whitelist), X-Instance-Identity (RSA pubkey b64), X-Hudson-JNLP-Port / X-Jenkins-CLI-Port (actual agent port — may NOT be 50000). This is the discovery path when the controller randomized its agent port; recce currently has no way to find those.

capabilities.name: x-instance-identity-fingerprint
capabilities.description: Base64-decode the X-Instance-Identity RSA pubkey, take SHA-256 of the DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo. This fingerprint uniquely identifies one Jenkins controller — the same value shows up on every port the controller listens on and on every agent that trusts it. Publish as a NEW cross-service shared surface (known_pubkey_fingerprints / known_jenkins_controllers) so scans of multiple subnets can prove 'these three hosts are one Jenkins farm' and so a captured agent secret can be attributed to the correct controller.

capabilities.name: jnlp4-tls-cert-capture
capabilities.description: PROTOCOL_JNLP4-connect wraps the channel in TLS with a self-signed cert whose CN/SAN carries 'Jenkins'. Complete the STARTTLS-style upgrade, capture the leaf cert, cross-check its pubkey against the X-Instance-Identity fingerprint above, and file the cert into services/probes.py's TLS store so cert-based correlation (services/probes.py cert_covers) covers Jenkins farms too.

capabilities.name: agent-name-enumeration-from-http
capabilities.description: When the HTTP controller has /computer/api/json readable (anonymously or with a known cred), harvest every agent's displayName + assignedLabels. Attempt a JNLP handshake using each name — a valid name gets a challenge, an unknown name gets 'Agent trust not established'. Yields the list of live agents even when the /computer/ UI is locked down. Feed harvested names into creds.known_users AND core.known_hostnames (Jenkins agents are usually named after their hosts).

capabilities.name: agent-secret-relay-attack
capabilities.description: If services/web/checks.py surfaces an unauthenticated /computer/{agent}/slave-agent.jnlp or a leaked /computer/{agent}/config.xml (both grant the 64-hex agent secret), open a fresh :50000 connection, negotiate JNLP4-connect, present the stolen (nodeName, secret) pair, complete the HMAC-SHA-256 challenge. The controller then dispatches remoting commands to us — arbitrary code execution in the controller's build-orchestration context, and file-read on any workspace the compromised agent had. Publishes the (controller_ip, agent_secret_b64) as a relay_targets entry so cli/_creds.py runs it exactly like it runs mssql/ldap relays today.

capabilities.name: hmac-challenge-capture-for-offline-crack
capabilities.description: In JNLP2/3 the server sends a challenge and expects HMAC-SHA-256(agent_secret, challenge). Capture both halves and emit a hashcat-ready line (mode 1450, HMAC-SHA-256 keyed by secret). Even on JNLP4 the inner challenge is HMAC-SHA-256 once the TLS is stripped in a controller-side capture. Published to creds.known_hashes for the normal hashloot / hashcat pipeline.

capabilities.name: cve-2024-43044-agent-file-read-detect
capabilities.description: Version-gate against the controller banner captured on the sibling HTTP port: Jenkins < 2.470 or LTS < 2.452.3 permits a compromised agent (or anyone completing the JNLP handshake, per the advisory) to invoke ClassLoaderProxy#fetchJar against arbitrary paths on the CONTROLLER filesystem — arbitrary file-read against JENKINS_HOME (secrets, credentials.xml, master.key). Emits a critical finding and a proof runbook.

capabilities.name: jnlp-network-exposure-finding
capabilities.description: Baseline reachability finding: an agent port reachable from a pentest-scope network segment is a misconfiguration on its own — Jenkins docs recommend the agent port be reachable ONLY from agent hosts. Analogous to zk_stat_reachable / db2_reachable. Records the negotiated protocol set as evidence.

capabilities.name: jnlp-runbook-emitter
capabilities.description: Emit a runbook the operator can copy-paste: `printf 'PROTOCOL_INVALID\n' | nc {ip} {port}` to dump supported protocols; `nmap -p{port} --script jnlp-info {ip}` (custom NSE) or Metasploit `auxiliary/scanner/jenkins/jenkins_udp_broadcast_enum` / `exploit/multi/http/jenkins_metaprogramming`. Mirrors zk runbook() / db2 runbook().

capabilities.name: controller-version-cross-link
capabilities.description: Once the sibling HTTP Jenkins version is known, propagate it back onto the agent-port Port record (port.product='Jenkins', port.version=<X>) so recce/vuln/vulndb.py's version-matcher fires the Jenkins CVE stack (2.319-, CVE-2024-23897, CVE-2024-43044) against the agent port too. Today the agent port has no product/version so it's invisible to the CVE mapper even when the HTTP twin is fully fingerprinted.

cross_service_wire_candidates: known_users (creds/known_users.py): agent nodeName strings harvested from /computer/api/json + successful JNLP handshakes — Jenkins agents are commonly named 'build-01', 'jenkins-worker', 'ci-runner' which double as OS/service usernames elsewhere on the network
known_hostnames (core/known_hostnames.py): agent nodeName often equals the agent host's short name; also X-Instance-Identity + cert SAN yield the controller's own hostname claim

known_hashes (creds/known_hashes.py): HMAC-SHA-256 challenge/response captured during JNLP2/3 negotiation → hashcat mode 1450 line for offline agent-secret cracking; also fingerprint of X-Instance-Identity RSA pubkey for correlation-only use

relay_targets (core/relay_targets.py): (controller_ip, controller_agent_port, nodeName, agent_secret) tuples — a stolen agent secret from an HTTP-side leak gets replayed against the JNLP port by cli/_creds.py exactly like mssql/ldap relays today

known_domains (core/known_domains.py): TLS SAN from the JNLP4 leaf cert and the controller's advertised URL in the tcpSlaveAgentListener response often disclose the internal DNS zone (e.g. jenkins.corp.internal)

NEW shared surface — known_pubkey_fingerprints / known_jenkins_controllers: SHA-256(SPKI(X-Instance-Identity RSA)) uniquely IDs a Jenkins controller across scans, ports, and IP changes. Same shape and consumer story as relay_targets — publish so any host serving the same fingerprint is auto-linked in the report as 'part of Jenkins controller X'. Would also let SSH/MSRPC-side host-identity clues attach to the same controller entity.

web/checks.py feedback loop: agent-port discovery on a non-standard port (X-Hudson-JNLP-Port header) tells the HTTP web-scanner to also probe /tcpSlaveAgentListener/ and /manage; conversely, web/checks.py's Jenkins version fingerprint propagates back onto the agent-port Port record so vuln/vulndb.py CVE-matches it (see controller-version-cross-link capability)
act/exploitplan.py: CLI2-connect detection produces a Metasploit-ready row (exploit/linux/misc/jenkins_command_receive) exactly like the current /script row
vuln/vulndb.py: publishes agent-port-specific CVE rows (CVE-2017-1000353, CVE-2024-43044) keyed on product=jenkins so version-matched findings fire on the agent port too, not just on HTTP

recommended_hashcat_modes.description: HMAC-SHA-256 (keyed by secret) — matches the JNLP2/3/4 agent authentication challenge/response; captured (challenge, response) pair cracks the 64-hex agent secret offline
Raw SHA-256 — matches the legacy JNLP1-connect 'hashed secret' form when a JNLP-connect handshake is observed

recommended_findings.title: Jenkins agent listener speaks CLI2-connect (CVE-2017-1000353 pre-auth Java deserialization RCE)
Jenkins agent port permits agent-secret relay from HTTP-side leak (full controller/workspace compromise)
Jenkins controller vulnerable to CVE-2024-43044 (agent -> controller arbitrary file read of JENKINS_HOME secrets)
Jenkins JNLP legacy plaintext protocol (JNLP-connect / JNLP2-connect) enabled — agent secrets transit in cleartext
Jenkins agent port reachable and 50000/tcp collision auto-resolved from Db2 to JNLP (misconfigured Db2 finding suppressed, real JNLP finding raised)
Jenkins agent names harvested via /computer/api/json + JNLP handshake probing (feeds known_users/known_hostnames)
Jenkins controller reachable via JNLP agent-listener from pentest scope (should be agent-network-only)
Jenkins X-Instance-Identity pubkey captured and fingerprinted (cross-scan controller correlation)
Jenkins JNLP HMAC-SHA-256 challenge captured and queued for offline hashcat mode 1450
Jenkins controller version propagated from HTTP twin onto agent-port record (CVE mapper now fires here)

implementation_notes:
Ship as recce/services/jenkins_jnlp.py, mirroring services/zookeeper.py's shape: is_jenkins_jnlp(port) classifier, targets(hosts), probe(ip, port) doing (a) protocol negotiation and (b) sibling-HTTP /tcpSlaveAgentListener/ fetch when a Jenkins HTTP port is present on the same host, findings(hosts, probes), runbook(ip, port), findings_to_vulns(fs) via svccommon, analyze(hosts, ...) driven by svcprobe.iter_probe.

The db2.is_db2() port-only True on 50000 must become protocol-gated — refactor to require the DSS 0xD0 magic in the EXCSAT reply before claiming the port. Add a small svcdetect.py signature entry ((r'^PROTOCOL_JNLP|^Protocol:JNLP', 'jnlp-agent', 'Jenkins JNLP agent listener')) plus a PORT_NAMES fallback pointing 50000 to a disambiguator function (NOT a hardcoded name).

Register serviceenum.py entries: _NAME 'jnlp-agent'->'jenkins-jnlp', 'jenkins'->'jenkins-jnlp' when portid==50000; leave the recce-service.sh driver script (scripts/recce-service.sh) to add a jenkins-jnlp lane that shells out to nc / a small python probe.

Add vulndb.py rows for CVE-2017-1000353 and CVE-2024-43044 keyed on product=jenkins so the version cross-link capability fires them.

Feed act/exploitplan.py with matcher r'jenkins.*cli2|cve-2017-1000353' -> exploit/linux/misc/jenkins_command_receive; matcher r'jnlp.*agent.secret.relay' -> a manual runbook (no MSF module — hand-rolled remoting client).

The NEW shared surface (known_jenkins_controllers keyed on SHA-256(SPKI)) is best placed alongside core/relay_targets.py — it is one file, one dict-of-sets, one write_* function, one reader — same footprint. Consumers: report/markdown.py + report/excel.py sections; and jenkins_jnlp.findings() itself uses it to auto-attach a finding to every host in the controller cluster.
